assumptions: Positively selected variants are likely to be recent and to have experienced fewer recombination events.
conclusion: Inference of recombination or selection may be confounded because both processes affect genetic variation.
scope: Motivation stated in the abstract; no formal identifiability result.
span: However, genomic variants subject to positive selection are likely to have arisen recently and, consequently, had less opportunity to be affected by recombination. Thus, the two processes have an intimately related impact on genetic variation, and inference of either may be vulnerable to confounding by the other.

objects: positive selection; population-based recombination rate estimates
assumptions: Modest positive selection in the settings illustrated by the authors.
conclusion: Even modest positive selection can substantially reduce population-based recombination rate estimates.
scope: Illustrated sensitivity of population-based recombination estimates; the abstract gives no quantitative conditions.
span: We illustrate here that even modest levels of positive selection can substantially reduce population-based recombination rate estimates.

assumptions: Human genome-wide scans for recent selection described by the authors.
conclusion: The concentration of reported selection loci in low-recombination regions suggests that recombination-rate confounding may have reduced scan power.
scope: Author interpretation of prior scans; the abstract names no specific earlier method.
span: We also show that genome-wide scans to detect loci under recent selection in humans have tended to highlight loci in regions of low recombination, suggesting that confounding by recombination rate may have reduced the power of these studies.

assumptions: Both pedigree-based and population-based recombination rate estimates are available.
conclusion: Ped/Pop detects selection genome-wide using the ratio of pedigree-based to population-based recombination rate estimates.
scope: The abstract defines the statistic and required estimates; it gives no likelihood, prior, null calibration or fitting procedure.
span: Motivated by these findings, we introduce a new genome-wide approach for detecting selection, based on the ratio of pedigree-based to population-based estimates of recombination rate.

objects: completed selective sweeps; neutral versus adaptive evolution; recombination rate; time after fixation
assumptions: Simulation settings used by the authors; Ped/Pop is designed to capture completed sweeps.
conclusion: Simulations suggest that Ped/Pop discriminates neutral from adaptive evolution, performs well at high recombination, and retains power for many generations after fixation.
scope: Simulation-supported performance statement; no theorem or parameter-specific power guarantee appears in the abstract.
span: Simulations suggest that our “Ped/Pop” method, which is designed to capture completed sweeps, has good power to discriminate between neutral and adaptive evolution. Unusually for a multimarker method, our approach performs well in regions of high recombination and also has good power for many generations after the fixation of an advantageous variant.
